verified.catalyst: California DFPI either reinstates its suspended approval of Western Union's $16.00/sh all-cash buyout of Intermex, after which the companies say they will close promptly, or the deal breaks or slips at the Nov 10, 2026 outside date.
verified.dated_milestone: The DFPI decision has no set date. The hard date is the Nov 10, 2026 outside date, after which either party may terminate (per the Aug 10 IMXI 10-Q, as press reports cite it). The parties could also agree to extend it. Next check: any DFPI reinstatement 8-K, or an outside-date amendment before Nov 10.
verified.instrument: IMXI common (NASDAQ), long against the $16.00 cash consideration. Option to hedge with WU short not needed (cash deal).
verified.bloom_gates: G1 (named counterparty: Western Union, signed merger agreement) + G2 (contractual $16.00 cash, NYDFS approval already granted 2026-08-13; DFPI is the last open approval) + G3 (a $3.33/sh, 26% spread that is visibly unpriced because the market puts roughly 40% odds on closing)
verified.edge: M. This is a clean binary on one regulator. The cash price is contractual, so the upside needs no provenance re-derivation. Undisturbed base: the $16 price was about a 50% premium to the 90-day VWAP, which puts the base near $10.67. Run-up from that base to today's $12.67 is +18.7%. Remaining to $16.00 is +26.3%. Downside to standalone value of about $10.4-10.7 (52-week low $10.355) is about -16% to -18%. Implied close probability is about 36-40%. Before the Aug 13 suspension the stock traded near $15.5 (200-day average $14.66), so most of the deal value has already been given back. The trade is not harvested; the residual is large. The edge exists only if the true close probability is above about 40%. Arguments for: DFPI already approved once, and its re-review cites the 6 months elapsed rather than a substantive objection; NY cleared under political pressure from the NYC mayor; both parties publicly committed. Arguments against: the DFPI 'impact on operations in this state' language is open-ended; California is Intermex's key growth market; there has been no public progress in 2 months.
verified.primary_source: Western Union 8-K Ex-99.1 / BusinessWire 'Western Union and Intermex Provide Update on Pending Acquisition' (2026-08-14, describing the DFPI letter dated 2026-08-13); Crowdfund Insider (2026-08) on the NYDFS approval; Nov 10 outside date per Intermex 10-Q filed ~2026-08-10 (as press reports cite it); FMP quote IMXI $12.67 (2026-10-12)
verified.kill_fact: Confirmed against primary sources (Business Wire/GlobeNewswire PR of 2026-08-13/14, WU 8-K exhibit): the $16.00 all-cash deal; NYDFS approval; the DFPI letter of 2026-08-13 suspending the extension it had granted on 07-31 'based on a need to further review the transaction'; and both companies saying they will close promptly once DFPI reinstates. IMXI is at $12.67 (FMP live), below its 50-day average of 12.98 and its 200-day of 14.66, against a 52-week high of 15.95. The spread widened after the suspension, so the market is pricing real break risk. Nothing has been published in about 2 months (no FMP news, PR or web hit after 08-14), so the trigger has not fired and has no date. The Nov 10 2026 outside date, its extension mechanics and the termination fee are all UNVERIFIED: I found no merger agreement termination article. The line's own claim that the timing is load-bearing therefore has no primary support. A DFPI 're-review' after 6 months, looking at California operations (Intermex's key growth market), points to conditions or remedies or a long slip rather than a quick reinstatement. A slip past an unverified outside date gives WU an option to walk, and Intermex has no confirmed reverse fee to protect it. The numerator is clean (cash consideration, no waterfall issue), and nothing has been harvested yet; the price sits about 26% below the deal price. The edge is legitimate, but the timing is unknowable and the fee is unconfirmed, so I cut it from 6 to 4. Corrections: the outside date and fee must be pulled from the merger agreement (8-K Ex 2.1, Aug 2025) before sizing, and the resolution may be a slip or extension rather than a binary outcome on Nov 10.
verified.analysis: Verified: WU/IMXI $16 all-cash deal (announced 2025-08-10). NYDFS approved 2026-08-13. That same day the DFPI suspended the extension of its approval that it had granted on 2026-07-31, citing the need to re-review after six months and the deal's effect on California operations. Both companies have said they will seek reinstatement and close promptly once it comes. IMXI is at $12.67 (FMP, 2026-10-12), a 26.3% gross spread with roughly 17% downside to standalone value, so the reward-to-risk is about 1.5:1 and the market implies about 38% odds. The gaps: I found no news after mid-August on whether DFPI has reinstated, whether the Nov 10 outside date has been or will be extended, or how large the termination fee is (the PR says only that fees 'could' apply). The trigger may therefore slip past Nov 10 rather than resolve, which is why the score is 6 rather than 7.
